items.text: Zakaj nista šla k marmalni hiši?
items.q: Ghassem, a boy, reuses the mispronounced word for marble that Maman used earlier. Does 'marmalni hiši' read as that same slip?
before: …kolo se je vrtelo. Bilo je rdeče. Kot tista velika rdeča vrata. Sedel sem ob jarku. Noge sem položil v jarek. Vode ni bilo. Srce sem imel prazno. Moški se je vrnil. Sprednje kolo se ni več vrtelo. Omidu je dal klofuto. Oba sva jokala. Moški je odšel. Ghassem se je vrnil. Grajal nas je. Rekel je:

items.text: Ne mislim tega. Mislim Alaina Kurčona. Kuuu-rac. Pika, konec.
items.q: Hooman mocks Eskandar's pout and drags out the rude word in the nickname. Does 'Kuuu-rac' land as a crude punch line?
before: – ... in oblikuješ usta kakor piščančja rit in se raztrguješ pri poskusu govoriti kakor on.

items.text: Kaj ti je spet, da si se nam nasršil, Alain Kurčon?
items.q: Hooman mocks a roommate for getting an erection at them, using his rude nickname. Is the crude joke clear?

items.text: Pazi, da ne počiš, gospod Kurčon.
items.q: Hooman shortens his rude nickname for Eskandar to 'gospod Kurčon' as Eskandar puffs himself up. Does this jab sound natural?

items.text: Ja, kupil ti bom punčko. Ko dobim denar, ti kupim še boljšo, Babova punčka.
items.q: The dad playfully echoes his toddler's baby talk. Does that come through?
before: – Vžžž, Baba, Baba, mi kupiš to veliko punčko?

items.text: Oh-ho. Hamid Mačka, včeraj si rekel khar. Zdaj si pa postal civilizirani in praviš osel?
items.q: Taghi teases Hamid: yesterday he used a blunt word for donkey, now he's gone all polite and says 'osel'. Does the jab work?

items.text: Je Arasteh prirejena oblika od araasteh, urejenega?
items.q: A guard jokes that the name Arasteh is a trimmed form of the Persian word araasteh, neat. Does this joke read naturally?

items.text: Če Bog da, naj bo vaš araasteh vedno urejen.
items.q: The guard ends with a friendly blessing that puns on the name: may you always be neat. Does it sound like a warm blessing?

items.text: Pravim tisto, da Ameroka pravi, da je Iran ustavil jedrski program. Pomeni to, da bo vojna ali ne?
items.q: Maman, worried about war, again says 'Ameroka' for America. Does the whole line sound like a mother from a small town?
Amir mishears the computer term 'pir tu pir' as 'Stari tu Stari', his own nickname. Does his mishearing come across?
before: – Neke vrste elektronski denar, pir tu pir.

items.text: Sinoči se je slišalo, kako prežvekuješ.
items.q: Eskandar mocks Hooman for secretly eating sweets at night, chewing like a cow chews cud. Does 'prežvekuješ' carry that jab?
before: Eskandar se je obrnil proti Hoomanu in rekel:

items.text: Prav, Orlov Pogled, prav. Zdaj pa ne tišči očal v prenosnik.
items.q: Hooman teases short-sighted Sajad, nicknamed Eagle Eye, for peering right into his laptop. Does this tease land?
She teases him by dropping in the English slang word 'sneaky'. Does it sound natural for a young woman to say this?
before: – Danes ste se sredi fakultete pogovarjale še z nekaj drugimi dekleti, slišal sem.

items.text: Karroubi je ljubezen, po resnici in pravici povedano.
items.q: Farid gushes about a politician he adores, adding his pet phrase 'in all truth and fairness'. Does this sound like an excited young man?
before: – Hej, Krčmar, teci. Teci, greva. Pravijo, da Karroubiija niso pustili na univerzo. Njegovi privrženci so zlomili vrata Hafez in vstopili. Na nek način bi lahko rekli, da so univerzo zavzeli.

items.text: Dal bi vse zate, Nini-jan. Tvoja glava tako dobro dela.
items.q: Amir fondly praises his mother, whom the family lovingly call Nini, for her quick wit. Does this sound warm and natural?

items.text: Super, Starešina Krčme. To je ravno prav za Arastehja.
items.q: Friends nickname Amir after a Hafez line about the wise old man of the tavern. Does 'Starešina Krčme' work as a nickname?
before: Hooman je odprl knjigo in rekel:
– Jaz sem služabnik Starešine Krčme, čigar milost ...
